doc.title: Josiah Gluck interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 13, 2022

title: Learning on the job after Johns Hopkins and Peabody
summary: He studied art history at Johns Hopkins, spent his time at the radio station, took a little Peabody class work, and learned mostly by doing.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: Did you learn all this mostly on the job?

A lot on the job. Well in college it was a nice linear progression because I went to Johns Hopkins as an art history and humanities major. Then I spent a lot of time at the radio station there and somewhere I could show you my GPAs so you could see just how much time I spent at the radio station. But I did do a little bit of class work at the Peabody Conservatory of Music which is now part of Hopkins but back then it was just this other place here in town. But they had a small recording set-up and the radio station — we got our blank tape from there and so forth. But most of what I’ve learned I’ve learned on the job. And so I’ve sort of come at it the other way where it’s not a lot of theory and then some practice in a recording program. I’ve been in the trenches pretty much from the get-
go. And any sort of electronics or electrical engineering my background is still very limited with that, but I’ve learned by doing.
Sounds like you have a future in the classroom someday.
